column1: # p858 2026-11-16 — T193 boundary test: when does a licence-hash collision mean a shared HOLDER?
# T193 was built on MIT payloads. MIT and BSD embed the holder name; Apache-2.0 and GPL do not.

column6: 6 others - AND A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION, DIFFERENT COUNTRY

column1: # 4 MIT payloads of ONE holder are byte-size-IDENTICAL at 1,066 B and hash DIFFERENTLY - the 4-digit year is the only difference.
# 7 Apache payloads across TWO organisations in TWO countries hash IDENTICALLY - because the appendix names nobody.
# So: a hash collision on a holder-bearing licence (MIT, BSD) is evidence about the holder.
#     A hash collision on a holder-agnostic licence (Apache-2.0, GPL) is evidence about the TEMPLATE and nothing else.
